the development of a theory of dynamic noninterference.

we have developed a mathematical basis to define dynamic noninterference and a method to check that a given program respects such a policy.
we propose a formal framework in which it would be possible to define dynamic interference policies and we show how it is possible to enforce them in a sound way.
we propose a framework to model dynamic interference policies and we give an algorithm to check the safety of a program with respect to a dynamic interference policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we provide a mathematical framework to reason about dynamic interference policy, which is a very useful notion to model security properties of programs.
it allows to reason about the evolution of confidentiality policies and to express dynamic policies in the form of a program.
